packages.label: יִחוּדָא עִלָּאָה וְיִחוּדָא תַּתָּאָה
packages.label_en: Upper and Lower Unification — The Two Modes of Covenant
packages.reason: This package contains all concepts that are expressions of the two modes of divine unity (yichuda ila'a = Shabbat union; yichuda tata'a = weekday union) and their structural equivalents. They share the essential nature of brit/covenant: the two forms of conjugal holiness (Shabbat-to-Shabbat and weekday-within-Torah-law), the halakha/kabbalah pair (lower and upper mystery), Metatron who mediates the weekday, the grasses (small people) and trees (great people), and the divine name Shaday. All are expressions of the same underlying reality: the boundary (tzimtzum) between domains that constitutes holy union.
nodes: מי שהוא שומר הברית, שזווגו משבת לשבת
הנהגת הקדוש ברוך הוא בששת ימי החל
מי שזווגו בששת ימי החל, ואף על פי כן הוא שומר את בריתו על פי התורה, שאינו יוצא מדיני התורה

merge_notes.reason: The upper covenant (brit ila'a) IS the sun (proof: 'brit ila'a she-hu bechinas hashemesh'). This pair is the Shabbat-level brit, a direct expression of yichuda ila'a.

The Tabernacle in its building-state IS the 39 lights. This is the positive pole of the brit: one who guards the covenant, his 39 labors are like the Tabernacle's construction — full of holy light. This is the reward-side of yichuda/brit.

From the source text (§7): 'tzvi latzaddik' means the beauty of holy conjugation. It contains both razin (halacha = yichuda tata'a) and razin d'razin (kabbalah = yichuda ila'a). The essential nature is the same as the whole package: holy conjugal union.

packages.label: פְּגַם הַבְּרִית
packages.reason: This package contains all expressions of covenant violation and its consequences. They share the essential nature of 'tosafot' — the forbidden addition/overflow that violates the boundary of holiness. The verse 'arbaim yakenu velo yosif' (40 lashes, not one more) IS the brit violation: going beyond what is permitted. The destroyed Tabernacle and the 39 lashes are two faces of the same damaged reality. This is the exact evil mirror of Package 1.

merge_notes.reason: From the source text (§4 context): one who violates the covenant draws upon himself the yoke of livelihood — the 39 labors (melacha) become a burden, and this burden produces sadness (atzvut). The source text explicitly states the 39 melachot are what the covenant-violator draws upon himself instead of the 39 lights. Depression (atzvut) is a state that characterizes this domain — it IS the experience of the 39 melachot as burden.

packages.label: דִּבּוּר הַמֵּאִיר
packages.label_en: Illuminated Speech — The Bird Between Water and Heaven
packages.reason: This package contains all concepts that share the essential nature of illuminated speech (dibbur ha-meir) and its fruits. The tzipparta (bird) IS speech; it stands ankle-deep in the water (man, who is made of male and female waters) and its head reaches heaven (the deep understanding of Torah). Speech illuminates the places where one needs to do teshuvah. Straw (teven) IS understanding (tevuna); heaven (shamayim) IS the deep insights of Torah; ירקא IS teshuvah; ירקא שקל IS teshuvat ha-mishkal. All of these are two faces of the same reality: the transformative power of verbalized Torah — speech that raises man from his lowly state toward Torah depth.

merge_notes.reason: Man (adam) IS water (mayim) — he is formed from male and female waters (mayim duchrin and nukvin). This pair identifies the 'lower realm' in which the bird of speech stands: the water = mankind in its lowly state. Bechina: they are two names for the same reality (man's material constitution).

In the Moshe–Yochani exchange: 'teven ata machniss la'afrayim' — straw (teven) is a bechina of tevuna (deep understanding, Binah). This is an explicit bechina in the source text (§1, line 5). It belongs in this package because straw/tevuna is what illuminated speech delivers to the lowly (afar = dust).

Heaven (shamayim) IS the deep insights of Torah — the bird's head reaching heaven means speech bridges man up to Torah depth. The proof in the source text cites the metzora narrative: 'yavo pattataya vikhaper al pattataya.' This is the height that illuminated speech reaches.

Yraka (green herbs / the word וַיָּרֶק — he armed/stirred) IS teshuvah. From Midrash Bereishit Rabbah 43: Avraham 'armed' his disciples in the portion of Shofetim, which is about teshuvah. This is the destination that illuminated speech leads to: the places that need teshuvah are lit up by speech.

Yraka shekul (measured/weighted herbs) IS teshuvat ha-mishkal (precise, weighed repentance). This is a deeper or more complete form of the same repentance concept as ירקא/תשובה — two levels of the same teshuvah domain.

packages.label: גֵּאוּת וַעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה
packages.label_en: Pride and Idolatry — The Evil Mirror of Covenant
packages.reason: Pride (gaavah/gadlut) and idolatry share the same essential nature: both claim that God is insufficient ('ein dai be'elokuto'), both represent the antithesis of the Shaday consciousness (she-yesh dai be'elokuto). The Torah explicitly equates gaavah with avodah zarah in §2–3. This is the evil mirror of Package 1: if Package 1 is the domain of Shaday (divine sufficiency, covenant, boundary), Package 4 is the domain of the one who rejects divine sufficiency and goes beyond the boundary.
